resources.string: Shows or hides the Developer options screen in Settings. Turning it off also turns off both debugging switches, as Settings does.
Lets a computer connected over USB use ADB. A new computer still has to be authorized on this phone.
ADB over Wi-Fi (pairing still required). Needs an active Wi-Fi connection; Android switches it back off when Wi-Fi drops.
WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS is granted. The switches below apply immediately, and three Quick Settings tiles are available in the tile editor.
Android only lets an app change these settings if it holds WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS, which cannot be requested with a dialog. Grant it once with any option below. It survives reboots and app updates.
From a computer with ADB (USB debugging has to be on for this one step):
Or on this phone, without a computer:
This also turns off USB and wireless debugging. Any computer connected through either will be disconnected.
A computer connected over USB will be disconnected.
A computer connected over Wi-Fi will be disconnected. If that is the connection you are using right now, it drops too.
Not connected to Wi-Fi. Wireless debugging needs a network.
Wireless debugging is off, or its address has not been announced yet. Turn it on from the Switches tab.
Shizuku is running. Allow DevSwitch to use it, then pairing and the paired-computers list work here.
Shizuku is installed but not started. Start it, then reopen this tab.

Generating a pairing code needs the shell identity, which DevSwitch gets through Shizuku, the same way it grants its own permission. Set up Shizuku on the Switches tab, or pair from Android\'s own screen.
Pair a computer over Wi-Fi. Show a code to type into adb pair, or scan the QR that Android Studio shows.
If this is the computer you are connected through, that connection drops and it will have to pair again.
Scanned Android Studio\'s code. Finishing the pairing on this device.
On the computer run this and enter the code. In Android Studio, use Pair using pairing code, choose this device, and enter it.
Waiting for a computer to pair…
No other adb devices found. Devices show up here while their wireless debugging is on and they are on this Wi-Fi.
In Android Studio, open Pair using QR code, then point the camera at it.
That is not an Android pairing QR. Keep looking for the one Android Studio shows.
Camera permission is needed to scan the QR.
Lost contact with Shizuku, so pairing stopped.
Pairing timed out. Start again to retry.
Could not start pairing. Shizuku took too long to respond.
Could not start pairing. Shizuku\'s service did not respond. Is Shizuku still running?
Could not start pairing. The adb service is not reachable on this device.
Could not start pairing. Not permitted. Check that Shizuku access is still allowed.
Could not start pairing. See the log for details.
